text:
mike: heads-up — seeing a cluster of NVRM Xid errors on rack-r12 GPUs in us-west-2 over the last 24h. primary codes: Xid 13 and Xid 31. correlates with heavy decode workloads (text-gen-large, batch=64).

anna: ack. which driver + kernel?

mike: nodes report driver 515.86 and kernel 5.15. dmesg snippets show repeated entries: 
```
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 13, pid=4421, 0x1b5f3a0 0x20000000 0x0, Xid64=0x000000000000000d
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 31, pid=4483, channel 0000000000000042
```

kartik: exact racks? any hostnames?

mike: r12-*-gpu nodes: r12-03, r12-07, r12-11. all in us-west-2a. timestamps cluster around 03:12-03:20 and 06:18-06:40 UTC.

jess: infra-bot created a short report: /links/incident/1912345001. added ECC counts and nvml telemetry. 

infra-bot: telemetry dump linked: s3://redwood-infra/telemetry/1912345001/ (ECC, power, temp, PCIe resets).

anna: ECC counters? temperature?

mike: ECC single-bit rising on r12-07 (from 0 to ~120 over 24h). temps normal: 62-68C. power stable. PCIe resets seen on r12-11.

kartik: Xid 13 historically -> illegal memory access during kernel init or hw fault, often seen with overclock/thermal/power glitches. Xid 31 -> channel timeout during heavy async workloads (KV cache/chunked decode). both together suggest intermittent bus or firmware trouble.

nina: any pattern by workload id? which models were scheduled?

mike: yes — high correlation with text-gen-large decodes and embedding-batch-64 concurrent jobs. batcher logs show continuous 64-sized batches during peak.

jess: quick mitigations: reduce batch size to 16 for suspect nodes, toggle continuous batching off for those queues, and force node drain for r12-11. can someone run kubectl drain?

kartik: running `kubectl drain r12-11-gpu --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` now.

mike: thanks. also capture nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,utilization,power for the nodes before reboot.

anna: pulled nvidia-smi and nvml logs, saved. attached small dmesg excerpt:
```
[Mar 18 03:16:12] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 13, 0x00000002
[Mar 18 03:16:13] pci 0000:af:00: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Corrected, type=Physical Layer
[Mar 18 03:16:14] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 31, channel 0x42
```

mike: looks like corrected PCIe errors precede Xid 13. could be flaky riser or slot. r12-11 had a small bump in PCIe CRC errors.

nina: do we have swap history for hardware? is this card recently moved?

mike: r12-07 got a GPU swap 6 months ago; r12-11 is original. r12-03 never swapped. all three started failing within same 48h window.

kartik: hypothesis: workload pattern created sustained KV-cache pressure + large batches -> increased memory activity -> surfaced marginal silicon + PCIe noise -> Xid 13/31. Plan: (1) drain suspect nodes (r12-11) and run memtest/cuobjdump (2) change default batcher policy to cap at 32 for text-gen-large for us-west-2 region for 24h (3) push driver update candidate 525.60 to a canary host with same kernel (4) schedule GPU physical inspection for riser/slot on maintenance window.

jess: i'm on patching. creating canary group of 2 nodes in us-west-2a with driver 525.60 and kernel 5.15. will run synthetic decode loop for 6h and watch Xid counts.

sre-oncall: created incident INC-2026, assigned eng-infra. logging runbook: collect /var/log/nvidia-installer.log, /var/log/dmesg, nv-hostengine dumps, and core if present.

anna: while patching, enable persistent NVRM logging: `echo 1 > /proc/driver/nvidia/params/LogVerbose` and set `NVRMLogLevel=10` in node config for suspects. also enable `GPU_USE_SYNC_OBJECTS=1` in runtime for a test group to reduce async channel churn.

mike: good call. jess — keep canary pinned and run embedding-batch-64 and text-gen-large with synthetic traffic to reproduce. for real workloads reduce batcher concurrency by 30% for all us-west-2 nodes.

jess: canary now running synthetic workload. initial 1h: no Xids yet. I'll escalate if appears.

kartik: concurrently, create a metric alert: if Xid13_count > 3 in 15m on any node, auto-mark node as drain_candidate and notify #eng-infra.

nina: for ROI/cost: if throttling reduces throughput by ~20% we estimate extra infra cost ~$3.5k/day on busy region. worth trading against unscheduled replacements. flagging finance if sustain >72h.

mike: agreed. prefer short-term perf hit over data-plane failures.

jess: update — after 5h canary still clean. r12-11 shows recurring PCIe CRC noise even after reflow. scheduled physical swap for 03/20 maintenance.

anna: flagged cards with vendor RMA team (ticket RMA-8812). attached part numbers and s/n.

infra-bot: RMA ticket RMA-8812 created, ETA 7-10 business days for replacement parts.

mike: checklist for post-replace: verify ECC counters reset, run 12h synthetic, validate PCIe CRC zero for 24h, then migrate production back to default batching.

nina: please cc finance on extended rolling replacements. I'll open cost tracker.

jess: will keep thread updated. closing for now but will post after swap and driver canary results. :thumbsup:

mike: thanks everyone. summary: throttle batchers in us-west-2, canary driver + synthetic tests, drain + replace r12-11 (scheduled), RMA open, metric alert created.
